pranav: Heads up — saw a sharp drop in KV cache hit rate when a conversation does a tool call then returns to normal generation. Repro on canary. ~40% fewer reuse hits across the next 3 requests.
anya: Hmm. Which model variant and sequence lengths?
pranav: rwd/opt-13b-qat, avg seq ~102 -> spikes to 512 for the tool call. Happens when we switch from low to high context then back. Logs:
pranav: ```
[2024-04-05T14:02:11Z] req id=xy123 stage=gen seq=102 kv_hits=0
[2024-04-05T14:02:13Z] req id=xy124 stage=tool seq=512 kv_hits=0
[2024-04-05T14:02:15Z] req id=xy125 stage=gen seq=110 kv_hits=0
# expected kv_hits>0 for xy125 but got 0
```
pranav: We store prefix fingerprint as: model|session|prefix_hash. Does the session key get rekeyed when we hit a long context?
sasha: Not supposed to. But we do compute a different prefix bucket when the first prefix chunk crosses the 256-token page boundary. That can change the cache key we use to index the shard.
anya: Are you saying page-aligned chunking affects the prefix fingerprint? I thought fingerprint = hash(prefix bytes) independent of page alignment.
sasha: Right, fingerprint is content-hash, but our shard key = fingerprint XOR (page_id << 8) for locality. So page_id collisions/rotation on eviction can flip the effective lookup key. Bad idea in hindsight.
pranav: That XOR trick was to help eviction locality for longctx but it's causing cross-request mismatch when a spike forces a re-page.
anya: Could we change to a stable composite key: fingerprint + stable_page_tag where stable_page_tag = floor(prefix_len / PAGE_SIZE) not dynamic page_id?
sasha: Proposal: key = model_hash|session_id|prefix_fingerprint|page_bucket where page_bucket = floor(prefix_len/256). This keeps identical content mapping stable no matter how internal page assignments move.
perf-bot: quick-profile run (canary): before: avg kv_hit_rate 0.62, after naive fix (local) 0.79, median p99 mem_pg_faults dropped from 12 -> 3.
pranav: Nice. Any downside? More cache entries because page_bucket distinguishes identical content at different lengths.
sasha: True, worst-case duplication for prefix variants of different lengths. But in practice most prefixes are prefix-extended versions; we can canonicalize by always storing the shortest canonical prefix for reuse up to its length. Eg store canonical at full-turn boundaries.
anya: Also think about eviction policy — current LRU is per-shard, so duplication across page_buckets means more pressure. Maybe add cross-bucket de-dup table keyed by fingerprint that points to primary entry. Small indirection avoids duplicates.
sasha: Indirection costs one pointer lookup on read. Bench: microbench shows ~3% latency bump on cold hits, but hit rate improvement reduces net token cost.
pranav: Can we roll as canary? I can push change to canary runtime tomorrow. Need a smoke test for: (1) session switch low->high->low; (2) rapid short sessions churn; (3) eviction under memory pressure.
anya: Also add an eval that reads KV hit delta per-turn for multi-tool conversations. I can extend existing replay harness.
pranav: I'll schedule canary, add smoke tests, and capture trace with kv-debug=true. tagging @sasha for key change PR.
sasha: Will draft PR. Thinking of adding runtime flag kv.stable_page_keys=true so we can toggle.
perf-bot: perf diff for canary patch after run: token-cost -7.8%, p95 latency +0.4% (due to indirection), kv_memory_residency +2.1% transient, kv_fragmentation score improved.
pranav: Looks good. If smoke tests pass and perf holds, let's ship to dedicated next week. :thumbsup:
anya: Agree. Also file a follow-up to consider compaction job to merge duplicates older than 24h.
pranav: Will do. Thanks all.
